diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-1 Checking specific gravity
diagrams.description: Illustration of checking battery electrolyte specific gravity and temperature using a hydrometer and a thermal gauge inserted into the battery cells.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Insert hydrometer vertically into cell; ensure float moves freely without clinging to sides.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-2 Checking specific gravity
diagrams.description: Close-up diagram showing how to read the top level of the hydrometer float with scale at eye level.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Read the scale line aligned with the surface meniscus of the electrolyte.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-3 Charging condition
diagrams.description: Graph showing relationship between specific gravity at 20°C (68°F) (1.06 to 1.28) and charging condition percentage (0% to 100%). Lines indicate max charging specific gravity 1.28 and 1.26.
components: Graph curves for 1.28 and 1.26 specific gravity
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Recharge if battery charge condition is below 60% or specific gravity is below 1.20.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-4 Specific gravity at electrolyte temperature
diagrams.description: Nomograph chart for converting specific gravity at electrolyte temperature St (-10°C to 50°C) to converted specific gravity S20 (1.10 to 1.30).

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-5 Freezing point of electrolyte
diagrams.description: Graph showing the freezing point temperature of battery electrolyte (°C and °F) vs specific gravity (1.00 to 1.32), indicating the shaded freezing zone.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: A discharged battery will freeze and crack the case at normal winter temperatures.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-6 Reduction gear starting motor [S114-254]
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway illustration of the Hitachi S114-254 reduction gear starter motor highlighting the planetary/reduction gearing arrangement and brush placement.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pinion gear is located independently of armature; commutator and brushes are located on the pinion/reduction gear side.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-7 Circuit diagram of starting system
diagrams.description: Complete electrical schematic and harness wiring diagram of the starting system showing battery, fusible links, ignition switch, starting motor, inhibitor switch (A/T only), and ignition / inhibitor relay.

callouts.M: Manual transmission only / Solenoid motor terminal

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Note: (M) indicates M/T only; (A) indicates A/T only. Inhibitor switch prevents cranking unless A/T is in P or N.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-8 Reduction gear type starting motor
diagrams.description: Functional schematic diagram showing the internal electrical circuits (series coil, shunt coil, contacts) and mechanical linkages (shift lever, reduction gear, overrunning clutch, pinion gear) of the starter motor.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Plunger pulls in and closes movable contactor 6 across stationary contacts 5, cutting out pull-in series coil 10 while hold-in shunt coil 7 maintains engagement.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-9 Reduction gear type starting motor (S114-254)
diagrams.description: Exploded view diagram of the Hitachi S114-254 starter motor showing all individual components and assembly order.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pay attention to the position of dust covers, packing, O-rings, and adjusting washers during disassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-10 [Removing magnetic switch and center housing]
diagrams.description: Illustration of detaching the magnetic switch assembly and O-ring/torsion spring from the center housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Torsion spring can be pulled off magnetic switch after separating.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-11 Removing brush holder
diagrams.description: Hand illustration demonstrating how to lift the brushes and extract the brush holder assembly from the armature commutator.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Lift brush on negative side away from commutator surface to withdraw holder safely.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-12 Removing center housing
diagrams.description: Illustration of unscrewing bolts securing the center housing to the gear case and detaching the housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Detach center housing carefully to access pinion gear.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-13 Testing field coil for continuity
diagrams.description: Ohmmeter probes connected to the two positive terminals of the field coil inside the yoke to check for electrical continuity.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity check: conduction required; open circuit means replace
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If tester shows no conduction, field coil is open. Replace yoke assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-14 Testing field coil for ground
diagrams.description: Circuit tester probes applied between the starter yoke body and positive field coil lead to test for insulation breakdown / grounding.
measurements_and_specs: Ground test: high resistance / no continuity required
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If very little resistance is read, field coil is grounded. Replace yoke assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-15 Inspecting brush spring tension
diagrams.description: Spring scale hooked to the brush spring clip to measure pull tension at the moment of release from the brush.
measurements_and_specs: Spring tension: 1.6 to 2.0 kg (3.5 to 4.4 lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Read tension when spring just releases from brush. Replace if outside specification.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-16 Undercutting insulating mica
diagrams.description: Diagram illustrating proper vs incorrect undercut profiles and depth of commutator segment insulating mica using a file.

callouts.Correct: Proper square cut 0.5 to 0.8 mm deep

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Undercut must be square at bottom, not V-groove. Deburr copper segments slightly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-17 Testing armature for ground
diagrams.description: Circuit tester probes placed between armature shaft/core and commutator segments to detect short to ground.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Any continuity between any commutator segment and the core/shaft indicates a bad armature.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-18 Testing armature for short
diagrams.description: Armature mounted on a growler tester with a thin steel blade held over the core while slowly rotating to check for shorted windings.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If the iron blade vibrates or is attracted to the core, armature coil is shorted.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-19 Pinion and reduction gear overrunning clutch
diagrams.description: Exploded view showing the pinion gear shaft, reduction gear, spring, and washer of the overrunning clutch assembly.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pinion gear shaft must slide freely through reduction gear.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-20 Testing brush for ground
diagrams.description: Circuit tester probes applied across the brush holder plate between positive and negative sides to check for insulation breakdown.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity indicates ground short (replace brush holder)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Ensure positive brush holder is properly insulated from the base plate.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-21 No-load testing
diagrams.description: Wiring hookup schematic for starter motor no-load test showing 12V battery, high-capacity ammeter (0-1000A), switch, voltmeter, and starter motor terminals S, B, and E.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Connect switch between battery positive and starter 'S' terminal; monitor current draw and RPM.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-22 Circuit of magnetic switch assembly test
diagrams.description: Circuit schematic for testing the starter magnetic switch pull-in: positive battery connects through switch to S terminal, negative battery connects to M terminal.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Connect negative battery to M terminal and positive through switch to S terminal to actuate plunger.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-23 Measuring clearance "l"
diagrams.description: Illustration of measuring pinion gap clearance 'l' between pinion energized position and manual pull-out stop against reduction gear.

callouts.Clearance l: Gap difference between electric stroke and full hand stroke

measurements_and_specs: Clearance l: 0.3 to 1.5 mm (0.012 to 0.059 in)
Adjusting washer sizes: 0.5 mm (0.020 in), 0.8 mm (0.031 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust clearance by adding or removing washers under magnetic switch mounting.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-24 Simplified charging circuit (1)
diagrams.description: Simplified circuit schematic (1) showing initial excitation state with ignition switch ON and engine stopped: current flows from battery through charge lamp to rotor coil and Tr1 to ground.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Charge warning lamp is illuminated because battery voltage passes through lamp to terminal L and Tr1 to ground.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-25 Simplified charging circuit (2)
diagrams.description: Simplified charging circuit schematic (2) with alternator running below regulation voltage: stator supplies rotor current via sub-diodes D7-D9; voltage at L equals B so charge lamp turns OFF.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Equal voltage across charge lamp extinguishes bulb while alternator self-excites through D7-D9.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-26 Simplified charging circuit (3)
diagrams.description: Simplified charging circuit schematic (3) when battery voltage exceeds specified setpoint: Zener diode ZD conducts, turning ON Tr3, which turns OFF Tr1 and stops rotor field current.
measurements_and_specs: Regulated voltage threshold triggers ZD conduction
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tr3 ON shorts base of Tr2/Tr1 to ground, cutting off field current until voltage drops below threshold.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-27 Circuit diagram of charging system
diagrams.description: Comprehensive wiring harness schematic of the Datsun 280Z charging system including alternator, IC voltage regulator, battery, fusible links, fuse block, ignition switch, ignition relay, and bulb check relay.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bulb check relay connects charge lamp circuit during cranking for bulb verification.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-28 Alternator
diagrams.description: Exploded view diagram of the Hitachi LR160-42 alternator with built-in IC regulator showing all internal and external components in order of assembly.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Contains 9 total diodes: 3 positive, 3 negative, and 3 trio/sub-diodes mounted on heat sink plates.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-29 Separating front cover
diagrams.description: Illustration of alternator through bolts removed and separating front cover with rotor from rear cover with stator.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tap front bracket lightly with wooden mallet to split housings.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-30 Removing pulley and fan
diagrams.description: Exploded illustration of pulley nut, spring washer, pulley, fan, and spacer being removed from the rotor shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Hold rotor in vise with soft jaws to prevent scratching pole pieces when breaking nut loose.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-31 Removing rotor
diagrams.description: Illustration showing removal of rotor assembly from the front cover after removing bearing retainer setscrews.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove bearing retainer screws before pressing rotor out of front bearing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-32 [Pressing rear bearing onto rotor shaft]
diagrams.description: Arbor press fixture used for installing or supporting the rear bearing on the alternator rotor shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Apply force only to bearing inner race when pressing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-33 Pulling out rear bearing
diagrams.description: Bearing puller tool attached to pull the rear bearing off the rotor slip ring shaft.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Take care not to gouge or damage copper slip rings with puller jaws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-34 [Disconnecting stator leads]
diagrams.description: Technician using a soldering iron and needle-nose pliers to unsolder stator coil lead wires from the diode plate terminals.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Perform soldering/unsoldering as quickly as possible to avoid overheating silicon diodes.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-35 [Removing brush assembly and diode holder]
diagrams.description: Exploded view showing screws and mounting positions for brush assembly with IC regulator and diode holder in the rear cover.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect diode wires with soldering iron before loosening screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-36 Continuity test of rotor coil
diagrams.description: Multimeter / circuit tester probes applied across both slip rings of the rotor to test for continuity through the field coil.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity must exist across slip rings
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If there is no continuity, field coil is open. Replace rotor assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-37 Testing rotor coil for ground
diagrams.description: Circuit tester probes applied between slip ring and rotor iron pole core to check for short to ground.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If continuity exists, rotor coil or slip ring is grounded; replace rotor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-38 Testing stator for continuity
diagrams.description: Ohmmeter probes testing continuity between the different phase leads of the disconnected stator winding.
measurements_and_specs: Continuity must exist between all phase leads
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If no continuity between individual terminals, winding is broken; replace stator.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-39 Testing stator for ground
diagrams.description: Tester probe connected to stator lamination core while other probe contacts each winding lead wire to ensure no ground fault.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If any winding lead conducts to the laminated core, stator coil is grounded; replace stator.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-40 [Auxiliary diodes]
diagrams.description: Diagram showing the physical location of the trio auxiliary (sub) diodes mounted on the brush assembly plate.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Sub-diodes supply excitation field current to rotor once alternator is spinning.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-41 Conductive direction of diode
diagrams.description: Illustration of diode polarity markings: Black mark indicates current flows from terminal to case; Red mark indicates current flows from case to terminal.

callouts.Black: Direction of current: terminal to case
callouts.Red: Direction of current: case to terminal

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Black marking = reverse polarity / positive plate; Red marking = forward polarity / negative plate.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-42 [Checking positive diode]
diagrams.description: Checking positive diodes on SR holder plate using ohmmeter probes between plate case and individual diode terminals.
measurements_and_specs: Conduction in forward bias only; no conduction in reverse bias
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Conduction should occur only when tester negative probe is on terminal and positive on case.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-43 Checking diode
diagrams.description: Checking negative diodes pressed into the rear cover using ohmmeter probes between rear housing and diode terminals.
measurements_and_specs: Conduction when tester positive is on terminal and negative on case
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Negative diodes conduct in the opposite probe configuration from positive diodes.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-44 Checking diode
diagrams.description: Testing the sub-diodes on the brush holder using ohmmeter test probes across the diode terminals.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diodes must conduct in one direction only. If conducting both ways or neither way, replace.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-45 Removing sub-diode
diagrams.description: Using needle-nose pliers as a heat sink on diode lead while unsoldering the sub-diode terminal.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pinch diode lead with pliers to prevent destructive heat transfer to the silicon wafer.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-46 Brush wear limit
diagrams.description: Illustration of the alternator carbon brush and brush holder showing the stamped brush wear limiting line.

callouts.Brush wear limiting line: Limit line scored on brush body

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Replace brush assembly if brush is worn down to the limiting line.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-47 Measuring spring pressure
diagrams.description: Measuring brush spring pressure with a spring balance while the brush tip projects 2 mm (0.08 in) from the holder.
measurements_and_specs: New spring pressure: 255 to 345 gr (8.99 to 12.17 oz)
Rate of decrease: ~20 gr (0.71 oz) per 1 mm (0.04 in) wear
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure pressure when brush is projected exactly 2 mm from holder face.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-48 Tightening pulley nut
diagrams.description: Tightening the alternator pulley nut with a torque wrench while securing the rotor shaft.
measurements_and_specs: Pulley V-groove deflection limit: less than 0.3 mm (0.012 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check that V-groove runout/deflection is under 0.3 mm after torquing nut.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-49 Inserting brush lift
diagrams.description: Two-panel illustration showing how to push the brushes up and retain them using a brush lift wire inserted through the rear cover access hole, and then releasing it.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Insert wire from outside to hold brushes retracted during assembly. When withdrawing wire, push towards center to prevent damaging slip ring.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-50 Testing alternator
diagrams.description: Wiring test diagram for on-vehicle alternator performance test showing connection of voltmeter between BAT terminal and ground (E).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn headlights on high beam before running test. Do not exceed 1,100 rpm during initial test, and do not race engine.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-51 IC voltage regulator
diagrams.description: Front and rear view of the integrated circuit (IC) voltage regulator unit attached to the brush holder, showing terminal markings E, F, L, S, B and model stamping TRIZ-27 12V.
components: Terminals E, F, L, S, B
measurements_and_specs: Regulator stamp: TRIZ-27 12 V FAB026 684 BSLFE
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Unit is permanently sealed; if defective, replace entire IC regulator and brush assembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-52 Circuit of regulator
diagrams.description: Internal electronic circuit schematic of the IC voltage regulator showing terminal connections B, S, L, F, E, transistors Tr1, Tr2, Tr3, zener diode ZD, thermistor Rh, and biasing resistors.
components: Resistors R1, R2, R3, R4, R5
Terminals B, S, L, F, E
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Thermistor Rh compensates regulated voltage based on ambient temperature.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-53 Testing regulator
diagrams.description: Wiring test setup for IC regulator bench testing steps 2 through 5, showing two 12V batteries, 10-ohm resistor R1, variable resistor Rv, voltmeters V1, V2, V3, V4, and terminals E, F, L, S, B.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Stop test if resistors become excessively hot. Terminal S connected to center tap of Rv.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-54 Testing regulator
diagrams.description: Characteristic graph showing acceptable band of voltage V4 (V) on Procedure (5) (13.0 to 15.5V) versus regulator case temperature (-30°C to 110°C / -22°F to 230°F).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Regulated voltage decreases with increasing temperature due to internal thermistor compensation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-55 Testing regulator
diagrams.description: Modified circuit schematic for step 6 test of the IC regulator with terminal S disconnected from Rv and connected to BAT1.
measurements_and_specs: V4 must be 0.5 to 2.0V higher than in step 5
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Verifies regulator sense circuit switching behavior.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-56 Ignition system circuit diagram
diagrams.description: Functional circuit diagram of the contactless ignition system showing primary and secondary circuits, connections between the battery, ignition switch, starter, ignition coil, transistor ignition unit, distributor reluctor, pick-up coil, rotor head, and six spark plugs.
wiring_and_connections: Battery positive to ignition switch and starter
Ignition switch to ignition coil primary winding and transistor ignition unit
Pick-up coil signal wires to transistor ignition unit
Secondary winding high tension wire to distributor rotor head
Distributor cap terminals to spark plugs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pick-up coil detects reluctor tooth pass and triggers the transistor ignition unit to open coil primary current, collapsing magnetic flux to fire secondary spark.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-57 Ignition system circuit diagram
diagrams.description: Detailed electrical system wiring diagram showing full vehicle connections between fusible link, battery, engine earth, ignition switch, distributor, terminal block, condenser, ignition coil (+ and - terminals), and transistor ignition unit with wire colors.
wiring_and_connections: BW : Black with white stripe (Switched power)
WR : White with red stripe (Battery feed)
L : Blue (Ignition coil negative to transistor ignition unit)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Color codes: B = Black, BW = Black with white stripe, WR = White with red stripe, R = Red, G = Green, L = Blue. Condenser connects to BW lead at ignition coil (+).

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-58 Exploded view of distributor
diagrams.description: Exploded view diagram of the complete contactless distributor assembly showing internal and external components numbered 1 through 18.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: The contactor on the breaker plate is used to eliminate vacuum advance hysteresis. Reluctor is keyed to the shaft with a roll pin.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-59 Checking air gap
diagrams.description: Measurement illustration showing a flat feeler gauge inserted into the air gap between a reluctor tooth and the pick-up coil pole piece.
measurements_and_specs: Air gap: 0.2 to 0.4 mm (0.008 to 0.016 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Loosen pick-up coil screws to adjust gap to 0.2-0.4 mm (0.008-0.016 in).

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-60 Removing pick-up coil
diagrams.description: Procedure illustration showing removal of screws securing the pick-up coil assembly and harness within the distributor housing.
wiring_and_connections: Distributor harness disconnected at terminal block
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect distributor harness at terminal block prior to removing securing screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-61 Removing vacuum controller
diagrams.description: Removing the two retaining screws securing the vacuum controller assembly to the distributor body.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Detach vacuum controller after removing the two securing screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-62 Removing breaker plate setscrews
diagrams.description: Using a screwdriver to unscrew the setscrews retaining the breaker plate assembly inside the distributor.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove breaker plate setscrews to take out the breaker plate.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-63 Removing knock pin
diagrams.description: Driving the knock pin out of the distributor drive pinion gear using a hammer and small pin punch.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Punch knock pin out to detach the lower drive pinion.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-64 Removing rotor shaft and drive shaft assembly
diagrams.description: Withdrawing the rotor shaft and drive shaft sub-assembly upward out of the distributor housing.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Slide the combined rotor shaft and drive shaft out of housing once pinion is removed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-65 Removing rotor shaft
diagrams.description: Unscrewing the internal rotor shaft setscrew from the top cavity of the rotor shaft with a screwdriver.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Mark rotor shaft and drive shaft first; remove packing from top of rotor shaft to access setscrew.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-66 Cam-to-contactor clearance
diagrams.description: Diagram illustrating clearance adjustment between the distributor shaft cam lobe and contactor arm on the breaker plate.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Adjust cam-to-contactor clearance to exactly 0.3 mm (0.012 in) after reinstalling contactor.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-67 Driving in roll pin
diagrams.description: Diagram showing correct rotational orientation of the reluctor roll pin with its longitudinal slit facing outward.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always drive in roll pin with its slit toward the outer end of shaft. Always use a new roll pin.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-68 Transistor ignition unit circuit diagram
diagrams.description: Functional block diagram of the transistor ignition unit internal sub-circuits and wiring connections to the starter, ignition switch, battery, ignition coil, and distributor.
wiring_and_connections: Power switching circuit connected to ignition coil (-)
Lock preventing circuit and duty control circuit connected to power switching
Distributor pick-up leads to spark timing signal monitoring circuit
Ignition switch lead connected to starter and coil (+)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Unit contains power switching, duty control, spark timing monitoring, and lock preventing circuits.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-69 External view of ignition unit
diagrams.description: Perspective view of the transistor ignition unit casing and multi-wire plug connector showing the push-release latch.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Located on right-hand dash side panel in passenger compartment. Push latch of connector to remove.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-70 Checking power supply wiring and battery
diagrams.description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between terminal BW (+) and terminal B (-) of the disconnected transistor ignition unit harness connector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn on ignition switch before measuring. Full battery voltage must be present across BW and B.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-71 Checking primary circuit
diagrams.description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between terminal L and terminal B on the disconnected transistor ignition unit connector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Checks primary coil circuit continuity through the ignition switch and coil primary winding to connector terminal L.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-72 Checking ignition coil assembly
diagrams.description: Measuring resistance across the positive (+) and negative (-) primary terminals of the isolated ignition coil using an ohmmeter on x 1 range.
measurements_and_specs: Criterion: Approx. 0 ohm is OK; more than 1.8 ohm is N.G.
wiring_and_connections: Engine room harness disconnected from coil
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect engine room harness before checking resistance across (+) and (-) terminals.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-73 Checking pick-up coil
diagrams.description: Connecting an ohmmeter (Resistance: x 10 range) between terminals G and R on the disconnected transistor ignition unit connector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pick-up coil resistance must be approximately 720 ohms. Far less or more indicates faulty coil.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-74 Checking pick-up coil power signal pulse
diagrams.description: Connecting a circuit tester on AC 2.5-volt range across terminals G and R while cranking the engine with starter motor.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect cold start valve harness before test. The needle should deflect slightly while cranking.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-75 Checking pick-up coil power signal pulse
diagrams.description: Connecting oscilloscope positive probe to terminal R and negative probe to terminal G of the ignition unit harness connector.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Set SLOPE switch to positive. Crank engine and observe generated waveform.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-76 Wave form of pick-up coil
diagrams.description: Oscilloscope waveform comparison of pick-up coil signal: continuous full line represents normal (OK), dashed line or absence represents abnormal (N.G.).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: A full smooth sine-like waveform confirms normal pick-up coil signal generation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-77 Checking operation of transistor ignition unit
diagrams.description: Connecting oscilloscope positive lead to ignition coil (-) terminal and negative lead to body metal ground.
wiring_and_connections: Oscilloscope positive probe to coil (-) terminal
Oscilloscope negative probe to body ground
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Tests transistor unit primary switching by monitoring primary voltage waveform at coil negative terminal.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-78 Wave form of pulse
diagrams.description: Oscilloscope voltage waveform traces: pattern (a) displays a proper high-voltage induced primary spike (OK); pattern (b) displays a deformed/flat pulse (N.G.).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pattern (a) confirms proper switching transistor operation. Pattern (b) indicates internal transistor unit defect.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-79 Wave form of duty pulse
diagrams.description: Oscilloscope trace illustrating duty cycle measurement at engine idle, showing conduction time t, total cycle period T, and formula t/T x 100 = 8 to 20%.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure at engine idle speed. Duty ratio must be within 8% to 20%.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-80 Checking lock preventive circuit
diagrams.description: Connecting a DC voltmeter (50-volt range) between the ignition coil (-) terminal and body metal ground to check the lock preventive circuit.
measurements_and_specs: Expected voltage: Power source (battery) voltage as soon as switch is turned ON
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When ignition switch is turned on without cranking, tester should immediately read battery voltage, verifying primary current cut-off.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-81 Wave form of lock preventive circuit
diagrams.description: Oscilloscope voltage trace showing rapid rise from 0V up to power source (battery) voltage immediately upon turning ignition switch ON.
measurements_and_specs: Voltage level: 0V to Power source voltage
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Waveform must sharply transition to full battery voltage upon switch closure, confirming lock prevention cut-off.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-82 Wiring diagram for item (1) (Power supply wiring and battery check)
diagrams.description: Schematic highlighting in bold the power feed and ground circuit for test Item 1: from battery positive through fusible link and ignition switch to connector terminal BW, and from connector terminal B to earth ground.
wiring_and_connections: BW: Black with white stripe (Switched battery feed)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bold traces illustrate the exact supply and ground paths tested during Item 1 power supply verification.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-83 Wiring diagram for item (2)-1 (Checking primary circuit)
diagrams.description: Schematic highlighting in bold the primary ignition circuit path for test Item 2-1: battery positive, fusible link, ignition switch, ignition coil (+) and (-) terminals, through lead L to the disconnected ignition unit connector.
wiring_and_connections: L: Blue (Coil - to connector pin L)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bold lines show the complete circuit path tested when verifying primary coil voltage at connector pins L and B.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-84 Wiring diagram for item (2)-2 (Checking ignition coil assembly)
diagrams.description: Schematic highlighting in bold the isolated ignition coil assembly for test Item 2-2 coil internal resistance measurement.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bold lines highlight the ignition coil alone, isolated from vehicle harness for primary winding testing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-85 Wiring diagram for item (3) (Pick-up coil continuity check)
diagrams.description: Schematic highlighting in bold the distributor pick-up coil circuit for test Item 3: distributor pick-up coil, terminal block, and red (R) and green (G) wires connecting to the ignition unit harness plug.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bold lines highlight the signal wiring from distributor pick-up coil through terminal block to connector terminals G and R.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-86 Wiring diagram for item (5) (Transistor ignition unit check)
diagrams.description: Schematic highlighting in bold the complete operating transistor ignition unit and all interconnected circuits during dynamic testing (Item 5).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bold lines show all connected harnesses and components active during Item 5 unit functional testing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-87 Correct installation of high tension wire
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional drawing showing proper seating of the high tension wire terminal and protective rubber cap onto the ignition coil secondary tower.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Push rubber cap fully down so there is zero clearance between rubber cap and coil cap to prevent arcing.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-88 Sectional view of ignition coil
diagrams.description: Internal cross-sectional cutaway view of the oil-filled ignition coil showing all 12 numbered internal and external parts.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Case is oil-filled for optimal heat radiation and insulation; cap is made of arc-resistant alkyd resin.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-89 Spark plug
diagrams.description: Visual comparison showing spark plug electrode condition under four operating states: Normal, Carbon fouled, Overheating, and Worn.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diagnose combustion and heat range from spark plug appearance. Use hot plug for short trips, cold plug for continuous high-speed/towing operation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EE-90 Setting spark plug gap
diagrams.description: Using a wire feeler gauge and bending slot tool to measure and adjust the spark plug side ground electrode gap.
measurements_and_specs: Standard plug gap: 1.0 to 1.1 mm (0.039 to 0.043 in)
Canada plug gap: 0.7 to 0.8 mm (0.028 to 0.031 in)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Measure with a round wire feeler gauge. Always reset gap by carefully bending the ground electrode; never bend the center electrode.

troubleshooting.corrective_action: Remove starting motor and make test.
Inspect brush spring tension or repair brush holder.

troubleshooting.symptom: Alternator output below 12.5 Volts during on-vehicle test
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Alternator out of order (faulty IC regulator, open/grounded rotor coil, damaged stator coil, open/shorted diodes, worn brushes)
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Remove and check alternator condition; inspect diodes, rotor, stator, and IC regulator.
Correct or replace brushes and brush springs.
Retighten or solder connections. Replace leads if necessary.
Check regulator operation and repair or replace as required.

troubleshooting.probable_cause: Poor grounding of alternator and voltage regulator "E" terminal.
Broken ground wire (color of wire is black.)

troubleshooting.corrective_action: Correct or replace brushes and springs if necessary.
Check regulator operation and repair or replace as required.
